name: Hank Fry
life: “I still remember cards my mother displayed facing the wall.” People around Breakwater Way know Hank by a small Saturday habit. Hank stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I sell lighthouse cards printed inland. I asked the crew to show me their view from the bunk.
appearance: Hank is easy to recognize by short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in a black overshirt with pearl buttons with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light, Hank holds eye contact until the other person has finished when listening.
personality: Hank has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To stock a view from the crew bunks.
family: Merritt Hart is Hank’s second cousin. Hank calls about good news first. Merritt is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The missing name on the stern*, Merritt says, “I thought I was hiring a painter. The apprentice taught me to say the owner's name without flattening the last sound.”
connections: Edgar Joseph. An onboard drawing gives the souvenir seller an alternative to the hotel view.
